_comment: Reviewed exceptions to project/scripts/check_runners.py. Each entry names the rules it waives and why. Remove an entry when its workflow is fixed; the check warns about entries nothing uses.

entries.reason: Handle passing PRs: pull_request_target/workflow_run job with a write token in one manet-auto-merge concurrency group; a newer trigger replaces a queued or running sweep (cancel-in-progress true). Stays hosted with a 6-hourly fallback cron ('N */6 * * *') until the merge pipeline thread ships its event-driven replacement.

Board build reusable workflow. runs-on picks [self-hosted, openwrt-build] for same-repo pull_request callers and for the build-full.yml schedule/workflow_dispatch caller (self_hosted input), and ubuntu-24.04 otherwise, so fork PRs and the signed release build stay hosted. The audit only accepts the event-guard form for workflows whose own triggers are all in SAFE_FOR_EVENT_GUARD; this one is workflow_call, and every caller (build-pr-*.yml, build-full.yml, build-release.yml, pr-gate.yml) triggers only on pull_request, schedule or workflow_dispatch.

Looks for an earlier green build of the same inputs (firmware #88). runs-on is the event guard `(github.event_name != 'pull_request' || HEAD) && Macs || 'ubuntu-24.04'`, so fork PRs stay hosted and the schedule/workflow_dispatch full build uses the Macs. Allowlisted for the same reason as the build job: the audit rejects the event form in a workflow_call workflow, and every caller of build-firmware.yml triggers only on pull_request, schedule or workflow_dispatch.
QEMU first boot and OTA test needs /dev/kvm, which the self-hosted runners do not offer (Studio VMs are ARM64). Read-only token; runs after the self-hosted x86-64 build (firmware #79, 2026-11-04).
QEMU three-node mesh test needs /dev/kvm, which the self-hosted runners do not offer (Studio VMs are ARM64). Read-only token; runs after the self-hosted x86-64 build (firmware #94, 2026-11-07).

QEMU three-node mesh test needs /dev/kvm, which the self-hosted runners do not offer (Studio VMs are ARM64). Read-only token; nightly cron, once a day, on the newest 24.10 x86-64 image (firmware #94, 2026-11-07).

Pause board builds on hold: pull_request_target label job with an actions:write token that never checks out PR code; hosted like the other token-holding automation. Runs one at a time per PR in event order on purpose (cancel-in-progress false) so a pause is never dropped behind a resume.
Upstream label-triggered workflow at @main; its jobs skip unless a ci:kernel:* label is added.
Upstream label-triggered workflow at @main; its jobs skip unless a ci:target:* label is added.

Hosted on purpose: the merge job holds a write token and must not share a persistent self-hosted runner with jobs that run PR code, until dedicated JIT runners exist. Its single global manet-auto-merge concurrency group cancels in progress so a stuck run cannot starve later runs.

Builds dump1090-fa and dump978-fa natively and needs root apt-get for Boost, SoapySDR and ncurses headers. The ghostnet-linux-arm64 runners set no-new-privileges, so sudo fails there (packages #33 run, 2026-11-03). Path-filtered to decoder package changes, 15-minute timeout, cancels superseded PR runs.
